assumptions: The service avoids custody, regulated execution, and speculative certificate trading.
Qualified importers experience enough forecast variance to value recurring support.
Specialist carbon and trade review can be purchased economically.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid importer diagnostics showing quantified working-capital or error savings, conversion to recurring retainers, and a signed customs-channel agreement with clear advisory boundaries.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: CBAM turns emissions data into a recurring working-capital exposure, creating a useful bridge between compliance and treasury.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Certificate spend and penalty exposure are concrete, but customers may keep treasury decisions internal and demand for outsourced non-custodial coordination is unknown.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Prepaid retainers and diagnostics offer reasonable cash conversion, but analyst review, partner fees, liability costs, and an assumed 180-customer scale weaken confidence in owner economics.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: CEE declarants are identifiable, but the 50-tonne threshold reduces the smaller-importer pool and the addressable qualified segment is not quantified.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Customs brokers, accountants, Big Four advisers, and ERP vendors are naturally positioned to bundle forecasting and reconciliation.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: The workflow could expand into procurement analytics, supplier emissions management, customs compliance, and broader carbon-cost forecasting.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Importer-specific history and rules provide some switching friction, but the declarant retains control and the advisory provider is explicitly replaceable.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Combining emissions evidence with cash forecasts is useful, but no quantified savings or superior outcome versus internal teams and brokers is demonstrated.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The definitive regime and certificate exposure create a current catalyst for diagnostics and workflow formation.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Broker and finance-adviser referrals are plausible, yet those partners can also deliver the service themselves and no channel commitment is present.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A software-first, non-custodial start is feasible alongside employment, but legal boundaries, verified emissions inputs, liability, and specialized trade knowledge remain material.

highest_value_structural_change: Embed the forecasting workflow inside a customs broker's recurring import process under a durable co-selling or white-label agreement.
main_structural_strength: It ties a mandatory compliance process directly to recurring cash exposure rather than selling generic sustainability reporting.
primary_score_limiter: The proposed provider controls neither certificate execution nor customer relationships and has no evidence that declarants will outsource treasury coordination.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Customers may retain treasury internally because they retain liability, while simplified thresholds shrink the smaller-importer market.
